en.bio1: Logan (Ngāti Pu) uses computational models to study how climate variability alters ocean stratification.
en.bio2: His interests extend to pursuing Earth system questions with practical importance, and to exploring open problems in pure mathematics.
en.paper0: A real counterexample to the Drury permanent conjecture
en.paper1: The four-dimensional Borsuk number is five or six
en.paper2: Petty’s conjecture holds in Lₚ for 2 ≤ p ≤ 4: d+1 equidistant points in every dimension d
en.paper3: Equilateral sets in ℓₚⁿ beyond n+1: Linear excess and dimension cost
en.paper4: A counterexample to Kusner’s conjecture on equilateral sets
en.paper5: A 32-leaf tree requiring six coordinates for an isometric ℓ∞ embedding

mi.bio1: Ka whakamahi a Logan (Ngāti Pu) i ngā tauira rorohiko hei rangahau i te pānga o te rerekētanga o te āhuarangi ki te hanga paparanga o te moana.
mi.bio2: Ko ōna aronga ko te whai i ngā pātai mō te pūnaha o te Ao e whai take ana ki te ao tūturu, me te tūhura i ngā rapanga kāore anō kia oti i te pāngarau parakore.
mi.nextAngle: Te koki e whai ake nei
mi.paper0: He tauira whakahē me ngā tau tūturu ki te whakapae a Drury mō te per(A)
mi.paper1: Ko te tau Borsuk mō te ahu-whā he rima, he ono rānei
mi.paper2: Ka mana te whakapae a Petty i te Lₚ mō te 2 ≤ p ≤ 4: he d+1 ngā ira tawhiti ōrite i ia ahu d
mi.paper3: Ngā huinga tawhiti ōrite i te ℓₚⁿ kei tua atu i te n+1: te taikaha rārangi me te utu o ngā ahu
mi.paper4: He tauira whakahē ki te whakapae a Kusner mō ngā huinga tawhiti ōrite
mi.paper5: He rākau 32 ngā rau e matea ana kia ono ngā taunga mō tētahi whakaurunga tiaki-tawhiti ki te ℓ∞
